# Appendix A: Support Functions {#appndx_a}
## Data Helper Functions {#appndx_a.data_helper.functions}
\

### Data Loading

::: {.noteblock data-latex=""}
The complete source code of the functions described in this section is available in the the [Data loading](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/tree/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L5-L419) section of the [data-helper.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/tree/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L5-L419) script on _GitHub_.
:::

#### [load_image.list](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L80) Function {#func.load_image.list}
\

This is a core utility designed to recursively traverse a root directory passed in the [root_path](#func.load_image.list.args.root_path) argument, discover character-specific (or class-specific, in the terms of the project's multiclass classifier models) subfolders, load data from raw image files (downloaded from the [Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/vaibhao/handwritten-characters) platform) using a custom parsing function, the pointer to which is passed in the [fn.load_image.dat](#func.load_image.list.args.fn.load_image.dat) argument, filter out empty or invalid images, and organize everything into an `R` list object with the corresponding labels and file paths.

::: { #func.load_image.list.usage .sidebar }
##### [Usage](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-scripts/ds.train2trimmed_img.dat.R#L15)
\

```{r usage@load_image.list, eval=FALSE}
  train.img_dat.list <- load_image.list(root_path = img.train_root.dir,
                                        fn.load_image.dat = load.img_trimmed.dat,
                                        folder.list = NULL,
                                        char_files.max = NA,
                                        char_files.seed = NA,
                                        random_sample = FALSE)

```

::: {.noteblock data-latex=""}
In the *code snippet* above, a pointer to the auxiliary function [load.img_trimmed.dat](#func.load.img_trimmed.dat) described below in *this Section* is used as the value of the argument [fn.load_image.dat](#func.load_image.list.args.fn.load_image.dat).
:::
:::

::: { #func.load_image.list.args .sidebar }
##### Arguments
\

::: { #func.load_image.list.args.root_path .sidebar }
- **root_path:** The root directory path containing subfolders of images organized by character recognition classes; 

:::
::: { #func.load_image.list.args.fn.load_image.dat .sidebar }
- **fn.load_image.dat:** Pointer to a user-defined loading and processing helper function applied to each image file path (e.g., a function to read image matrices or binary arrays); 

:::
::: { #func.load_image.list.args.folder.list .sidebar }
- **folder.list:**  (Optional, *Character*, $NULL$ by default) Vector of specific subfolder names to process. If $NULL$, it defaults to all directories found inside the *root path* passed in the [root_path](#func.load_image.list.args.root_path) argument; 

:::
::: { #func.load_image.list.args.char_files.max .sidebar }
- **char_files.max:**  (Optional, *Integer*, $NA$ by default) Numeric value limiting the maximum number of files to load per folder (useful for subsampling or testing); 

:::
::: { #func.load_image.list.args.char_files.seed .sidebar }
- **char_files.seed:**  (Optional, *Integer*, $NA$ by default) Random seed used for reproducible sampling when [char_files.max](#func.load_image.list.args.char_files.max) is specified (ignored otherwise); 

:::
::: { #func.load_image.list.args.random_sample .sidebar }
- **random_sample:**  (Optional, *Boolean*, $FALSE$ by default) Boolean ($TRUE/FALSE$) indicating whether files within a folder should be sampled randomly ($TRUE$) or taken sequentially from the top ($FALSE$). 

:::
:::

::: { #func.load_image.list.details .sidebar }
##### Details
\

Below is the *step-by-step execution flow* of the function:

1. **File Path Discovery:** Internally invokes the [img.file_path.get_list](#func.img.file_path.get_list) user-defined helper function (described below in the [Image Processing](#appndx_a@img_proc) section) to gather a structured list of file paths from each target subfolder, applying optional maximum limits (passed in the [char_files.max](#func.load_image.list.args.char_files.max) argument), random sampling (depending on the value passed in the [random_sample](#func.load_image.list.args.random_sample) argument), and seed generation (if the [char_files.seed](#func.load_image.list.args.char_files.seed) argument value is not $NA$).

2. **Label Generation:** Extracts directory names from the file path list and converts them into a factor to serve as classification labels.

3. **Iterative processing of class directories:** Iterates through each directory, performing the following operations:
    a) **Batch Loading:** Calls the custom loader function (the pointer to which is passed in the [fn.load_image.dat](#func.load_image.list.args.fn.load_image.dat) argument) using the [map](https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/purrr/versions/1.2.0/topics/map) `R` function across all file paths in the folder.
    b) **Data Validation & Filtering:** Evaluates a validity check on the loaded image data. Specifically, it checks that the binary matrix elements sum to greater than zero, effectively filtering out blank, corrupt, or unreadable images.

4. **Consistency Checks:** Enforces a safety assertion to ensure that the filtered image list length strictly matches the corresponding filtered file path list length.

:::

::: { #func.load_image.list.value .sidebar }
##### Value
\

Structured list containing two primary components:
1. *Label list:* A factor of *class labels*;
2. *Image list:* A nested list mapping each *class folder* to its valid loaded *image data* and corresponding *file paths*.

:::

::: { #func.load_image.list.code .sidebar }
##### Source Code
\

The simplified version of the [source code](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L80)  function is shown below:
```{r func@load_image.list.s, eval=FALSE}
load_image.list <- function(root_path,
                            fn.load_image.dat,
                            folder.list = NULL, 
                            char_files.max = NA,
                            char_files.seed = NA,
                            random_sample = FALSE) {

  img.file_list <- img.file_path.get_list(root_path, 
                                          folder.list,
                                          char_files.max,
                                          char_files.seed,
                                          random_sample)
  
  label_list <- as.factor(names(img.file_list))
  img_list <- lapply(img.file_list, function(char.dir){
    
    img_dat.ls <- map(char.dir$file_path.list, 
                  fn.load_image.dat)
    
    valid.idx <- sapply(img_dat.ls, function(img.dat){
      mx.bin <- img.dat[1,,]
      mode(mx.bin) <- "numeric"
      
      sum(mx.bin) > 0
    })
    
    ls <- list(img.list = img_dat.ls[valid.idx], 
               fpath.list = char.dir$file_path.list[valid.idx])
    
    stopifnot(length(ls$img.list) == length(ls$fpath.list))

    ls
  })

  list(label.list = label_list,
       img.list = img_list)
}

```

::: {.noteblock data-latex=""}
The source code of the [](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L4) function is also available in the [Data processing functions](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L) section of the [data.helper.functions.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L) script on _GitHub_.
:::
:::

#### [img.file_path.get_list](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L421) Function {#func.img.file_path.get_list}
\

This function traverses *image directories*, collects *file paths* grouped by *folder* (representing *class labels*), and optionally limits, seeds, or randomly samples files for *dataset preparation*.

::: { #func.img.file_path.get_list.usage .sidebar }
##### [Usage](#L)
\

```{r data-helper@lXXX, eval=FALSE}

```

::: {.noteblock data-latex=""}
In the *code snippet* above, *this function* is called internally from the [outer_img.file_path.get_list](#func.outer_img.file_path.get_list) function described above in *this Section*.

In the *code snippet* above, a pointer to *this function* is passed in the [fn.load_image.dat](#func.img.file_path.get_list.args.fn.load_image.dat) argument to the [img.file_path.get_list](#func.img.file_path.get_list) function described above in *this Section*.
:::
:::

::: { #func.img.file_path.get_list.args .sidebar }
##### Arguments
\

::: { #func.img.file_path.get_list.args.root_path .sidebar }
- **root_path:** The root directory path containing subfolders of images organized by character recognition classes; 

:::
::: { #func.img.file_path.get_list.args.folder.list .sidebar }
- **folder.list:**  (Optional, *Character*, $NULL$ by default) Vector of specific subfolder names to process. If $NULL$, it defaults to all directories found inside the *root path* passed in the [root_path](#func.img.file_path.get_list.args.root_path) argument; 

:::
::: { #func.img.file_path.get_list.args.char_files.max .sidebar }
- **char_files.max:**  (Optional, *Integer*, $NA$ by default) Numeric value limiting the maximum number of files to list per folder (useful for subsampling or testing); 

:::
::: { #func.img.file_path.get_list.args.char_files.seed .sidebar }
- **char_files.seed:**  (Optional, *Integer*, $NA$ by default) Random seed used for reproducible sampling when [char_files.max](#func.img.file_path.get_list.args.char_files.max) is specified (ignored otherwise); 

:::
::: { #func.img.file_path.get_list.args.random_sample .sidebar }
- **random_sample:**  (Optional, *Boolean*, $FALSE$ by default) Boolean ($TRUE/FALSE$) indicating whether files within a folder should be sampled randomly ($TRUE$) or taken sequentially from the top ($FALSE$). 

:::
:::

::: { #func.img.file_path.get_list.details .sidebar }
##### Details
\

Below is the *step-by-step execution flow* of the function:

1. **Subfolder Discovery:** If the [folder.list](#) argument value is $NULL$ (the *folder list* is not provided), the function retrieves all subdirectory names inside the *root directory* (using the path passed in the [root_path](#) argument) and uses them as the *folder list* for further processing. Otherwise, the [folder.list](#) value is used.

2. **File Path Collection:** Next, it iterates through the *folder list* determined in the previous step, constructs the *full path* for each folder, and retrieves all file paths in that folder.

3. Capping and Sampling: If the value for the [char_files.max] argument is provided and does not exceed the folder's file count, the number of files to process is limited to that value. 
  1. In the latter case, further processing depends on the value of the [random_sample] argument. If it is TRUE, a sample of the size provided in the [char_files.max] argument is taken using a reproducibility seed offset by the folder's index if a seed is provided (the value of the [seed] argument is not $NA$). Otherwise, a top list of the size provided in the [char_files.max] argument is selected.
  2. Otherwise, the full list of file paths obtained in the previous step is used for the final result.



::: {.noteblock data-latex=""}
This is an auxiliary function that is used internally in the [](#) function as shown above in the [Usage](#func.img.file_path.get_list.usage) section of *this Description*.
:::
:::

::: { #func.img.file_path.get_list.value .sidebar }
##### Value
\

A named nested list where each element represents a subfolder, containing its root path and the file path list.
:::

::: { #func.img.file_path.get_list.code .sidebar }
##### Source Code
\

The [source code](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L421) of the function is shown below:
```{r src@img.file_path.get_list, eval=FALSE}
img.file_path.get_list <- function(root_path, 
                                   folder.list = NULL, 
                                   char_files.max = NA,
                                   seed = NA,
                                   random_sample = FALSE) {
  if(is.null(folder.list))
    # Scans the root path to find all available subfolders.
    folder.list <- dir(root_path)

  # Generates a file path list
  path_list <- lapply(folder.list, function(folder_name){
    # Constructs the full path and retrieves all file paths for the given folder name.
    file.root_path <- file.path(root_path, folder_name)
    folder.idx <- which(folder.list == folder_name)
    
    put_log("Function: `img.file_path.get_list`:
Getting file path list from the following char's root folders:
%1", file.root_path)

    fpath.list <- list.files(file.root_path, 
                             full.names = TRUE)
    
    fpath.len <- length(fpath.list)

    # If the number of files is limited and 
    # the total number of files in the folder exceeds the limit
    if(!is.na(char_files.max) && fpath.len > char_files.max){
      
      # If a seed is provided.
      if (!is.na(seed)) {
        # Applies a reproducibility seed offset by the folder's index
        set.seed(seed + folder.idx)
      }
      
      
      if(random_sample) {
        # Samples the files randomly
        file.idx <- sample(fpath.len, size = char_files.max)
      } else {
        # Selects the top file according to the specified limit.
        file.idx <- seq_len(char_files.max)
      }
      
      fpath.list <- fpath.list[file.idx]
    }
    
    put_log("Function: `img.file_path.get_list`:
%1 files in folder: %2", length(fpath.list), folder_name)

    list(root_path = file.root_path,
         file_path.list = fpath.list)
  })
  
  # Shortens the name of each list item to the first character of the folder name..
  names(path_list) <- folder.list |> substr(1,1)
  path_list
}
```

#### [load.img_trimmed.dat](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L) Function {#func.load.img_trimmed.dat}
\

This specialized utility function reads an image file, dynamically detects whether it contains nonzero pixel data, optionally trims whitespace or empty borders around the visual features using the [magick package](https://docs.ropensci.org/magick/index.html), and extracts its raw data matrix structure.

::: { #func.load.img_trimmed.dat.usage .sidebar }
##### [Usage](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-scripts/ds.train2trimmed_img.dat.R#L15)
\

```{r func@load.img_trimmed.dat.u, eval=FALSE}
  train.img_dat.list <- load_image.list(root_path = img.train_root.dir,
                                        fn.load_image.dat = load.img_trimmed.dat,
                                        folder.list = NULL,
                                        char_files.max = NA,
                                        char_files.seed = NA,
                                        random_sample = FALSE)
```

::: {.noteblock data-latex=""}
In the *code snippet* above, a pointer to *this function* is passed in the [fn.load_image.dat](#func.load_image.list.args.fn.load_image.dat) argument to the [load_image.list](#func.load_image.list) function described above in *this Section*.
:::
:::

::: { #func.load.img_trimmed.dat.args .sidebar }
##### Arguments
\

::: { #func.load.img_trimmed.dat.args.file_path .sidebar }
- **file_path:** Path to the image file to load. 

:::
:::

::: { #func.load.img_trimmed.dat.details .sidebar }
##### Details
\

Below is the *step-by-step execution flow* of the function:

1. ***Image Loading:*** The function begins by reading the image file from disk into memory as an object using [magick::image_read](https://docs.ropensci.org/magick/reference/editing.html).

2. ***Matrix Conversion & Validation:*** Converts the loaded image into a numeric matrix representation using the user-defined helper function [magick_img2matrix](#func.magick_img2matrix) described below in described below in the [Image Processing](#appndx_a@img_proc) section.

3. ***Image Validation & Conditional Cropping:*** Evaluates the matrix's maximum value to check whether the image is entirely blank or empty. If valid content exists (the maximum pixel value is greater than zero), it applies [magick::image_trim](https://docs.ropensci.org/magick/reference/editing.html) to automatically crop out uniform background borders or whitespace, centering the content around the core visual features.

4. ***Data Extraction:*** Finally, it extracts and returns the underlying raw pixel buffer data using the [magick::image_data](https://docs.ropensci.org/magick/reference/editing.html#details) helper function.

::: {.noteblock data-latex=""}
This is an auxiliary function, the pointer to which is passed in the [fn.load_image.dat](#func.load_image.list.args.fn.load_image.dat) argument to the [load_image.list](#func.load_image.list) function, as shown above in the [Usage](#func.load.img_trimmed.dat.usage) section of *this Description*.
:::
:::

::: { #func.load.img_trimmed.dat.value .sidebar }
##### Value
\

:::

::: { #func.load.img_trimmed.dat.code .sidebar }
##### Source Code
\

The [source code](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L287) of the function is shown below:
```{r func@load.img_trimmed.dat.s, eval=FALSE}
load.img_trimmed.dat <- function(file_path) {
  img <- magick::image_read(file_path)
  img.mx <- magick_img2matrix(img)
  img.trimmed <- img

  if (max(img.mx) > 0) {
    img.trimmed <- image_trim(img)
  }
  
  magick::image_data(img.trimmed)
}
```

:::

#### [magick_img2matrix](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L485) Function {#func.}
\

This is a lightweight utility that converts a [Magick Image object](https://docs.ropensci.org/magick/reference/editing.html#details) into a *normalized numeric matrix of pixel intensities*.


::: { #func.magick_img2matrix.usage .sidebar }
##### [Usage](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L294)
\

```{r data-helper@l294, eval=FALSE}
img.mx <- magick_img2matrix(img)
```

::: {.noteblock data-latex=""}
In the *code snippet* above, *this function* is called internally from the [load.img_trimmed.dat](#func.load.img_trimmed.dat) function described above in *this Section*.
:::
:::

::: { #func.magick_img2matrix.args .sidebar }
##### Arguments
\

::: { #func.magick_img2matrix.args.img .sidebar }
- **img:** A [Magick Image object](https://docs.ropensci.org/magick/reference/editing.html#details) (typically processed, resized, or filtered prior to conversion). 

:::
:::

::: { #func.magick_img2matrix.details .sidebar }
##### Details
\

Below is the *step-by-step execution flow* of the function:

1. ([Line 482](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L486)) ***Raw Binary Data Extraction:*** The function calls the [image_data] function to extract the underlying raw hexadecimal or integer byte-array buffer from the [Magick Image object](https://docs.ropensci.org/magick/reference/editing.html#details).
2. [(Line 483](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L487)) ***Color Channel Isolation:***
Slices the multidimensional array to isolate the primary color channel matrix. For grayscale or black-and-white pipeline images (as in our case), this captures the single intensity plane.
3. ([Line 484](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L488)) ***Data Type Conversion:*** Explicitly casts the extracted data array elements from raw/character bytes into a numeric data type, making mathematical operations possible.
4. ([Line 485](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L489)) ***Min-Max Normalization:*** Divides the entire matrix by 255 (the maximum 8-bit color intensity value) to normalize pixel values into a clean floating-point scale ranging from 0.0 (black/background) to 1.0 

::: {.noteblock data-latex=""}
This is a utility function used internally by the other user-defined functions, as shown in the usage example above in the [Usage](#func.magick_img2matrix.usage) section of *this Description*.
:::
:::

::: { #func.magick_img2matrix.value .sidebar }
##### Value
\

:::

::: { #func.magick_img2matrix.code .sidebar }
##### Source Code
\

The [source code](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L485) of the function is shown below:
```{r src@magick_img2matrix, eval=FALSE}
magick_img2matrix <- function(img){
  img.dat <- image_data(img)
  mx.bin <- img.dat[1,,]
  mode(mx.bin) <- "numeric"
  mx.bin /255
}
```

:::
